_provenance.notes: Pacific halibut (Hippoglossus stenolepis) is a long-lived flatfish — maximum recorded age is 55 years. Females live longer and grow larger than males. The IPHC age-structured stock assessment uses otolith (ear bone) samples from commercial and survey catches to determine age composition. A declining trend in the size and age of halibut at the same CPUE level indicates a younger, smaller average population — which is what was observed from 1990-2015. The stock is divided into 9 regulatory areas (2A-4D), each managed separately.

life_history.early_life: Larvae hatch in deep water (600-1500m), drift north, metamorphose at surface, settle to bottom as juveniles in shallow (<200m) areas
life_history.migration: Adult halibut migrate between summer feeding grounds (inshore shelf) and winter spawning grounds (deep ocean 600-1500m)
life_history.spawn_location: Deep water along the continental slope — primarily near Queen Charlotte Sound and the Canadian border area

annual.notes: IPHC. Large, old fish dominant — decades of lower fishing pressure.
IPHC. Declining as large fish are preferentially harvested.
IPHC. IFQ discussions begin partly due to size issue.
IPHC. IFQ implemented — quota per pound incentivizes larger fish but trend continues.
IPHC. Near crisis — average fish half the weight of 1960.
IPHC. Trough. TAC cuts steep. 'Big fish problem' well-documented in literature.
IPHC. Recovery beginning — older fish returning.
IPHC. Recovery in both abundance and average size.
IPHC 2024. Continued positive trend. Source: IPHC 2024 setline survey weight composition data.
